sections.heading: What Every El Paso Traffic Ticket Has in Common
paragraphs: A speeding ticket on I-10, a stop-sign ticket in the Lower Valley and a no-insurance citation on Montana Avenue look different, but legally they are the same animal: a Class C misdemeanor under the Texas Transportation Code, punishable by a fine of up to $200 for most violations plus court costs set by the court. There is no jail. What there is, in every case, is a conviction that the court reports to the Department of Public Safety if you pay the ticket — because paying is a guilty plea.

That conviction is what actually costs you. It sits on the driving record insurers pull at renewal, and a conviction may affect premiums depending on your history, carrier and other rating factors. Texas no longer uses the former Driver Responsibility Program points system, but DPS may suspend the license of a "habitual violator" — four or more moving-violation convictions arising from separate incidents within 12 consecutive months, or seven or more within 24 months (Transp. Code §521.292(b)); our explainer on the former points system covers what changed. The other thing every ticket has in common is that it is negotiable, and Robert Navar works these dockets across El Paso County.

sections.heading: The Three Outcomes We Work For on Every Citation
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance promptly. From then on the court communicates with our office, and the appearance date stops being a failure-to-appear risk. Then we pull the citation and look for leverage.

On the pretrial docket we negotiate for one of three results. The best is an outright dismissal — nothing reported, nothing on your record. The most familiar is deferred disposition under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45A.302 (formerly art. 45.051): you pay a court fee, stay violation-free for the deferral period the judge sets, and the case is dismissed without a conviction. Where a judge won't defer — high speeds, some school-zone cases, CDL holders, drivers who used deferral recently — we work for a reduction to a non-moving violation that insurers don't rate the same way.

sections.heading: Flat Fees by Court: $59 Municipal, $69 Everywhere Else
paragraphs: Our pricing is set by the court your ticket is in, not by the charge. Citations written by the El Paso Police Department go to El Paso Municipal Court and cost a flat $59 per ticket. Citations from the Sheriff, a constable or a DPS trooper go to one of the Justice of the Peace precincts, and tickets from the smaller cities go to Horizon City, Socorro, or the San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton municipal courts — all $69.

Additional citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons of $10 to $30 shown at checkout. The consultation is free, and an existing warrant is $35 for the first and $20 for each additional. Not sure which court you're in? The free ticket and warrant lookup finds it, and our courts hub explains how each one runs its docket.

sections.heading: How to Pick the Right Ticket Page
paragraphs: Start with the words on the citation. The most common is a plain speeding ticket; if the stop was in a flashing-light zone near a campus, see school zone speeding, which many judges treat more strictly. Ran a light at Mesa and Sunland Park, or rolled a stop in a neighborhood? That's the red light and stop sign ticket page. A phone in your hand on Loop 375 is a texting and cell phone ticket under Transportation Code 545.4251 or the city's hands-free ordinance.

Paperwork tickets have their own fixes. No insurance (FMFR) carries a higher fine range but is often dismissed with proof of coverage on the date of the stop; expired registration and inspection tickets can generally be dismissed once you renew within the statutory window. If you were stopped without a license, the distinction matters: no driver's license means you never had one or didn't have it with you, while driving while license invalid (DWLI) means it was suspended — and DWLI can climb to a Class B with a prior or no insurance.

Professional drivers should go straight to the CDL ticket page, because federal rules bar most deferrals for commercial license holders, or to trucking and DOT violations for logbook, weight and equipment citations. If a trooper wrote the ticket on I-10 or US-54, see DPS state trooper tickets — those go to JP court, not Municipal. And for anything that isn't a moving violation at all — a loose-dog citation, a noise ordinance, a city code case — the Class C misdemeanors and city ordinance page covers it.
This page is general information, not legal advice about your case. If none of the categories fit, call 915-503-1600; se habla español, and the consultation is free.

sections.heading: What to Have Ready When You Hire Us
paragraphs: Whichever ticket you have, the online form asks for the same few things, and photos from your phone are fine: the citation (both sides, so we can read the court and the appearance date), your driver's license, your insurance card, and any letter the court has already mailed. Each service page lists the topic-specific proof that helps. If a date has already passed, tell us; our warrants hub explains what happens next.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court if I hire you for a traffic ticket in El Paso?
faqs.a: Generally not. We file an appearance and handle the pretrial docket for you. You would only appear if the case went to trial, which is uncommon for a Class C ticket.

faqs.q: How much does a traffic ticket lawyer cost in El Paso?
faqs.a: A flat $59 per ticket in El Paso Municipal Court and $69 in Justice of the Peace, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts. Extra citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons, and the consultation is free. You can hire online and pay at checkout.

faqs.q: Is it better to just pay the ticket?
faqs.a: Paying is a guilty plea and a conviction on your driving record. A conviction may affect insurance premiums depending on your history and carrier, so for many drivers the $59–$69 fee is the more economical path — and the dispositions we pursue are aimed at ending the case with no conviction at all.

faqs.q: What if my court date already passed?
faqs.a: There is probably a warrant and a separate failure-to-appear charge, but it is fixable. See our warrants hub or call us the same day. Warrant recall timing depends on the court's docket; many El Paso courts act within days once an attorney files, but timing cannot be promised.
